s: As per the provisional results of the 11th Agriculture Census (2021-22), the number of operational holdings in Andhra Pradesh is:
x: Operational holdings in AP rose to 96.90 lakh from 85.24 lakh, even as the average holding size fell from 0.94 ha to 0.86 ha.
tq: More holdings, smaller size: 85 → 97 lakh, 0.94 → 0.86 ha.

s: For Kharif 2026, the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister issued which directive regarding crop insurance?
o: Only loanee farmers' paddy crop to be insured, with banks accountable
Only horticulture crops to be insured, with FPOs accountable
Every cultivated crop to be insured, with District Collectors accountable
Insurance to be made optional for all crops, with Mandal officers accountable
x: In July 2026 the CM ordered that every cultivated crop be insured for Kharif 2026, making District Collectors accountable for coverage.
tq: Every crop insured; Collector answers for it.

s: For Kharif 2026 crop insurance in Andhra Pradesh, the last dates for enrolment were:
o: 15 July for all crops; 31 July for paddy
31 July for all crops including paddy
31 August for all crops; 15 September for paddy
x: Kharif 2026 enrolment closed on 31 July, while paddy had a later deadline of 15 August.
tq: July-end for most; paddy gets till Independence Day.

s: Which farmers' organisation demanded that free crop insurance be restored in Andhra Pradesh after the shift to voluntary enrolment?
x: The AP Rythu Sangham demanded restoration of the free crop insurance scheme that operated during 2019-24.
tq: AP Rythu Sangham = AP's own farm body, wants 'free' back.

s: At the 236th State Level Bankers' Committee (SLBC) meeting of Andhra Pradesh in September 2026, the Chief Minister:
o: Announced a complete waiver of all crop loans
Pushed lagging banks to meet their lending targets
Ordered closure of all Regional Rural Banks in the State
Directed banks to stop lending to tenant farmers
x: At the 236th SLBC (Sept 2026), the CM pressed banks lagging behind to meet their lending targets.
tq: SLBC = banks' report card; CM chased the laggards.

s: Andhra Pradesh is regarded as a pioneer in lending to tenant farmers through which of the following?
x: AP pioneered tenant lending using Crop Cultivator Rights Cards (CCRCs), Joint Liability Groups (JLGs) and Rythu Mithra Groups (RMGs).
tq: Tenants get credit via cards (CCRC) and groups (JLG, RMG).

s: In May 2026, the opposition in Andhra Pradesh alleged that the State's promised Price Stabilisation Fund had been abandoned, citing that maize was being sold at:
o: ₹1,400–1,600 per quintal against an MSP of ₹2,400
₹2,400 per quintal against an MSP of ₹1,600
₹1,800–2,000 per quintal against an MSP of ₹2,441
₹2,400–2,600 per quintal, above the MSP of ₹2,225
x: Maize was sold at ₹1,400–1,600 per quintal, well below the MSP of ₹2,400, prompting allegations that the Price Stabilisation Fund had been abandoned.
tq: Maize: market ~1,500 vs MSP 2,400 — a ₹800+ gap.

s: The reach of which umbrella scheme for ensuring remunerative prices to farmers through procurement and price support was highlighted by PIB in August 2026?
x: PM-AASHA (Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay SanraksHan Abhiyan) is the umbrella price-support scheme whose reach PIB highlighted in August 2026. PMFBY is crop insurance, PM-KUSUM solar pumps and e-NAM an electronic market.
tq: AASHA = hope of a fair price (MSP support).

s: Under Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Policy 4.0 (2024-29), an 'Ultra-Mega' project is one with investment:
x: AP Industrial Development Policy 4.0 classes projects with investment above ₹5,001 crore as Ultra-Mega.
tq: Ultra-Mega starts just past ₹5,000 crore.

s: As stated by the Union MSME Minister in the Rajya Sabha in August 2026, outstanding MSME credit stood at:
o: ₹10 lakh crore, up from ₹3.835 lakh crore in 2014-15
₹38.35 lakh crore, up from ₹10 lakh crore in 2014-15
₹55.24 lakh crore, up from ₹20 lakh crore in 2014-15
₹28.35 lakh crore, up from ₹10 lakh crore in 2019-20
x: Outstanding MSME credit was ₹38.35 lakh crore, up from ₹10 lakh crore in 2014-15.
tq: Nearly 4x: 10 → 38.35 lakh crore.

s: ECLGS 5.0, announced in May 2026, is best described as a:
o: Credit guarantee scheme to support emergency credit lines for businesses including MSMEs
Scheme for crop insurance of kharif crops
Export subsidy scheme for large corporates
Interest subvention scheme for housing loans
x: ECLGS is the Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme, which guarantees emergency credit for businesses, mainly MSMEs; version 5.0 came in May 2026.
tq: ECLGS = Emergency Credit Line Guarantee; 5.0 in May 2026.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the MSME base of Andhra Pradesh?
o: About 20.77 lakh units, mostly in services
About 95.88 lakh units, mostly in agro-processing
x: Andhra Pradesh has about 20.77 lakh MSME units, the majority of them in the services sector.
tq: AP MSMEs ≈ 20.77 lakh, services-heavy.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to electricity tariff regulation?
o: CEA — State retail tariffs in Andhra Pradesh
x: CERC fixes tariffs for central generating stations and inter-State transmission, while APERC fixes State tariffs. CEA does technical planning and PNGRB regulates downstream oil and gas.
tq: Central/inter-State → CERC; State → APERC.

s: When the rupee crossed ₹96.2 per US dollar on 18-19 May 2026, it had depreciated since 1 January 2026 by about:
x: By 18-19 May 2026, the rupee was down 6.3% since 1 January 2026. The 5.4% figure refers to FY26 depreciation up to January.
tq: May 2026: 96.2/$, down 6.3% in the calendar year.

s: As of May 2026, the fixed reverse repo rate of the RBI was:
x: The fixed reverse repo rate stood at 3.35%. 5.00% is the SDF rate and 3% is the CRR.
tq: Fixed reverse repo 3.35% sits far below the SDF floor (5%).

s: In August 2026, the RBI announced that it would resume on-tap licensing for which category of banks?
x: In August 2026 the RBI resumed on-tap licences for Urban Co-operative Banks (UCBs).
tq: On-tap UCB licences back in Aug 2026.

s: Which was the first Regional Rural Bank in India?
x: Prathama Grameen Bank was India's first Regional Rural Bank.
tq: Prathama = 'first' in Sanskrit — the first RRB.

s: Which was the first Small Finance Bank to commence operations in India?
x: Capital Small Finance Bank was the first Small Finance Bank in India.
tq: Capital = first (capital letter starts the list).

s: Under its new provisioning framework, the RBI is moving from which approach to which approach?
o: From a 3-stage ECL model to a 2-stage incurred-loss model
From incurred-loss model to a 3-stage Expected Credit Loss model
From a 90-day overdue test to a 180-day overdue test
x: The RBI is shifting from the incurred-loss model to a forward-looking 3-stage Expected Credit Loss (ECL) model; the 90-day overdue test stays.
tq: Provide before the loss happens: incurred → expected.

s: After the terms of Urban Local Bodies (15 March 2026) and panchayats (4 April 2026) in Andhra Pradesh expired, these bodies came to be administered by:
x: Once the elected terms expired, AP's ULBs and panchayats were run by Special Officers, which also puts Finance Commission grants at risk.
tq: No elected body → Special Officer in charge.

s: As an expenditure-side deficit-reduction measure, ensuring that grants for the creation of capital assets are not diverted has been emphasised by:
x: The CAG and NITI Aayog have stressed checking that capital-asset grants are not diverted to other uses.
tq: Audit (CAG) + planning (NITI) watch capital grants.

s: Andhra Pradesh's Budget 2026-27 targets the revenue deficit and fiscal deficit, as a percentage of GSDP, at respectively:
x: Budget 2026-27 targets a revenue deficit of 1.1% and a fiscal deficit of 3.8% of GSDP; option A reverses them.
tq: RD smaller (1.1), FD bigger (3.8).
